references.text: Moses gave the command that the entire law should be read aloud to all Israel, including women, children, and foreigners, during the Feast of Tabernacles every seventh year.
Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the priests and the elders of Israel, who were to read it to the people.
All Israel, including leaders, elders, women, children, and foreigners, gathered together to make a covenant with the Lord.
Joshua was commanded to hold fast to the entire law that Moses had given and to meditate on it day and night.
Joshua read aloud all the words of the law, the blessings and the curses, just as they were written in the Book of the Law.
Ezra read the law to the whole assembly, including men, women, and all who could understand, a practice that reflects the reading during Joshua's time.
Moses emphasized that nothing should be added to or taken away from what the Lord had commanded, which Joshua followed by reading everything aloud.
